expectations.text: Identifies this as a saturator over an UNKNOWN-size set (finding the members IS the work; not enumerable up front)
expectations.evidence: "Archetype: Saturator." ... "the count is unknown up front — finding the members *is* the work, so this is a search over an unknown-size set, not a known queue."

expectations.text: Uses heterogeneous finders / multiple distinct search lenses rather than a single grep or one-shot search
expectations.evidence: "Frontier: heterogeneous *finders*, each searching a different way (by log-sink API, by grep pattern, by dataflow ... )"; §2 lists 8 distinct lenses (by-sink, by-pattern, by-dataflow, by-schema, by-serialization, by-config, by-diff, by-runtime).

expectations.text: Adversarially verifies each candidate with a separate agent (tries to refute it) before it counts as a finding
expectations.evidence: "Verify: a separate, adversarial agent tries to refute it ... and passes only if the finding survives"; "Verify contract (a *different* agent, adversarial). The verifier never sees the finder's reasoning."

expectations.text: Stop rule is K consecutive dry rounds with no new confirmed findings, and dedups against everything SEEN (not just confirmed)
expectations.evidence: "Stop predicate: DRY_ROUNDS = 3 consecutive rounds in which no lens surfaces a new confirmed finding"; "a candidate the verifier refutes is still written to seen ... dedup against seen, never against confirmed".

expectations.text: Does NOT model the task as a fixed queue or a one-pass search that stops after looking once
expectations.evidence: "a search over an unknown-size set, not a known queue"; "looping until none of them find anything new for 3 rounds, is a far stronger signal than one pass."
